AI turns in human-AI programming sessions (long event log)

Source: R/data.R
ai_long.Rd

ai_long is a coded dataset of the turns of an AI coding assistant in 428 human-AI pair-programming sessions across 34 projects, held between 5 February and 8 March 2026, one row per code. A turn (message) can carry several codes, in the order given by code_order. Each code is one of eight assistant actions (Ask, Delegate, Execute, Explain, Investigate, Plan, Repair, Report), grouped into three clusters (Action, Communication, Repair).

Timestamps have day resolution (midnight, UTC+2, of the session date), so the order of events within a day comes from order_in_session, which counts the human turns of the session as well and therefore has gaps. Use actor = "session_id" with order = "order_in_session" for one sequence per session, or time = "timestamp" to split sequences at changes of day.

Usage

ai_long

Format

A data.frame with 8,551 rows (codes) and 9 columns:

message_id

Integer identifier of the turn; the codes of one turn share it.

project

Project identifier, "Project_1" to "Project_34".

session_id

Session identifier, a 12-character hash.

timestamp

Integer Unix time in seconds (day resolution).

session_date

Date of the row, "YYYY-MM-DD".

code

The assistant action, the state of the sequence.

cluster

The cluster of the code.

code_order

Order of the code within its turn, from 1.

order_in_session

Position of the row in its session, counting human and AI rows together.

Source

Bundled example dataset. The same data are distributed with the Nestimate package as ai_long.

See also

prepare_input(), context_tree().

Examples

tree <- context_tree(ai_long, actor = "session_id",
                     order = "order_in_session", action = "code",
                     max_depth = 2)
state_frequencies(tree)
#>         state count proportion
#> 1     Execute  3258 0.38100807
#> 2 Investigate  2317 0.27096246
#> 3        Plan  1620 0.18945153
#> 4     Explain   524 0.06127938
#> 5    Delegate   295 0.03449889
#> 6      Repair   257 0.03005496
#> 7      Report   181 0.02116711
#> 8         Ask    99 0.01157759
common_pathways(tree, top = 5, depth = 2)
#>                  pathway depth count likely_next next_probability  divergence
#> 1     Execute -> Execute     2  1503     Execute        0.5522289 0.006393297
#> 2    Investigate -> Plan     2   921     Execute        0.4668838 0.004718142
#> 3 Execute -> Investigate     2   727        Plan        0.3438790 0.031815394
#> 4        Plan -> Execute     2   674     Execute        0.4569733 0.016165977
#> 5 Investigate -> Execute     2   532     Execute        0.5112782 0.007986774
#>   changes_prediction
#> 1              FALSE
#> 2              FALSE
#> 3              FALSE
#> 4              FALSE
#> 5              FALSE
